sections.html:
Roughly 25 miles south of Boston and 35 miles east of Providence, Bridgewater is a Plymouth County town of 28,633 people (2020 census), up 7.8 percent from 26,563 a decade earlier. It spreads over 28.2 square miles, with Brockton about five miles north.

The Taunton River flows through town, and much of the Hockomock Swamp Wildlife Management Area fills the west side, which means certain lots back onto wetland or conservation land. Named neighborhoods and villages include Stanley, Scotland Park, Pratt Town, Paper Mill Village and South Bridgewater. Two ZIP codes serve the town, 02324 and 02325.

Buyers weigh the street, the lot and the distance to Route 24, Route 18 or the train ahead of any neighborhood name.

The official name is still the Town of Bridgewater, yet a city style of government runs it. At an April 24, 2010 town election voters traded the Board of Selectmen and open Town Meeting for a nine-member Town Council, with three district seats and six at large. The Town Manager, Assessor and Tax Collector are appointed.

Permits, tax questions and records all run through the town offices at the center of town. For your bill, the assessor's page on bridgewaterma.gov is the place to confirm details.

Interstate 495 meets Route 24 in the southwestern corner, and just one mile of the interstate falls inside town limits. At the Town Common, Routes 18, 28 and 104 come together, and Route 104 reaches Route 24 by ramp. Rail riders use Bridgewater station, on the Bridgewater State University campus, on the MBTA Fall River/New Bedford Line. Flights leave from T. F. Green Airport near Providence and from Logan in Boston.

Anyone commuting to Boston, Brockton or Providence will measure the drive to Route 24 and the station, so point out both.

Heavy snow is the weather risk with a local example: in February 2015 snow brought down the roof of Mitchell Elementary and students moved to other buildings. A homeowner can face a smaller version of that, so inspectors for buyers often study the roof.

Wet ground is common near the Taunton River and the swamp. A lot close to water invites questions on basement moisture, sump pumps and flood history. Your own records answer those, and your insurer can speak to coverage.

Quarterly billing has been the practice since July 1, 2010, so there are four tax bills a year.

BillMailedDue
PreliminaryEnd of JuneFirst business day of August and November
ActualEnd of DecemberFirst business day of February and May

A preliminary bill is only an estimate, with no tax rate or assessed value on it. An actual bill lists the rate, the assessment, abatements, exemptions and earlier payments. Approval of the tax rate comes from the state, usually in December.

Selling mid-year raises the question of the current quarter, and whether it is paid at the table, so put it to your closing attorney. The assessor's online database holds the property record card for your address.

sections.h2: Rules that apply to a sale
sections.html:
Almost every sale meets two state rules. One is the deed excise tax: $2.00 per $500 of price or fraction of $500, set by Massachusetts General Laws chapter 64D, section 1, which exempts instruments where the state, a town or the United States is a party. The registry of deeds collects it as the deed is recorded.

The other is the alarm certificate. The Bridgewater fire department must confirm that your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the requirements for a sale. It schedules the inspection and charges a fee, so call once a closing date exists. Battery alarms over ten years old, or expired, are swapped for ten-year sealed photoelectric models with a hush feature.

The Mass.gov alarm page shows how to find the date on your alarms and which standard fits your house.

Pull together the deed, the latest tax bill, permit records and a list of repairs you know about. An inherited house adds probate papers, and a rented one adds the leases.

  1. Compare your bill with the schedule above and mark any unpaid installment.
  2. Find your property record card in the assessor's online database.
  3. Replace expired alarms, then book the fire inspection as soon as there is a closing date.
  4. Ask your attorney how this quarter's tax gets settled at the table.

Many Bridgewater sales involve a house nobody wants to fix up. With an estate, the probate papers show who can sign, so locate them before you call a buyer. With tenants, the leases tell a buyer what rent and terms they would inherit. With a house that sat empty, expect questions about the roof, the heating system and the basement.

A direct buyer takes these situations as they come. Cash Home Buyers does not ask you to clean out the house or fix anything before we make an offer, and the closing attorney still settles the tax, the recording and the excise tax at the table.

1. Gather the papers above and decide whether you want a listing, a private sale or a cash offer.
  2. If you take an offer, read the written terms for the price, the closing date and who pays which fee.
  3. Hand the offer to your closing attorney, who orders the tax figures and checks the title.
  4. Book the fire department alarm inspection as soon as the closing date is fixed.
  5. At the table the attorney pays off any mortgage and unpaid tax from your proceeds, the excise tax is paid, and the deed goes on record at the registry.

A traditional buyer adds a bank appraisal and a loan approval to this list, and often a list of repair requests after the inspection. A cash sale to Cash Home Buyers skips those steps. The tax payoff, the alarm certificate and the recording still apply, but fewer parties have to line up for the closing date.

If your tax bill is behind, say so when you call. The balance does not stop a sale, since it comes out of your proceeds, but your attorney needs the exact figure for the day of closing and should have it before you accept an offer.

Three routes are open: list, sell it yourself, or accept a direct cash offer. Listing tends to pay off for a house in good condition. Cash fits when the house needs repairs, has tenants, belongs to an estate, or you want to pick the closing date.

Cash Home Buyers will look at a Bridgewater house as it stands, with no cleaning or repairs. Set our written offer next to a listing estimate before choosing. Whoever buys will price in what they find, so collect your permits and repair history first.

faqs.q: What county is Bridgewater, MA in?
faqs.a: Plymouth County, about 25 miles south of Boston.

faqs.q: When are Bridgewater real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Estimates are due the first business day of August and November. Actual bills are due the first business day of February and May. Your bill confirms the dates.

faqs.q: Does Bridgewater require an alarm inspection to sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale or transfer of a home needs a certificate of compliance from the fire department, which charges a fee. Phone it when a closing date is set.

faqs.q: How much is the Massachusetts deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The statute, MGL c. 64D, s. 1, sets $2.00 per $500 of consideration or fraction of $500.

faqs.q: Is Bridgewater a town or a city?
faqs.a: In practice, both. Since the 2010 vote a Town Council has governed it, but the official name is still the Town of Bridgewater.
